title: Camera and virtual camera motion
purpose: Lifts real and virtual camera moves (Ken Burns zooms, pans, punch-ins, parallax, shake) with speeds, easing and alternation rules.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F1 at the first and last frame of a shot to measure scale change; F8 for punch-ins and shake; F5 on a corner region.
pitfalls: Reading subject motion inside footage as camera motion
Estimating zoom from text that animates separately
Stating a speed without the shot duration it was measured over

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.parameter: one IR parameter object (name, type, description, default, min/max or choices, derived_from)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F5: Per-frame motion in a region (mean absolute frame difference, 0-255): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "crop=iw:ih*0.15:0:0,tblend=all_mode=difference,signalstats,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=$WORK/diff.txt" -an -f null -  (drop the crop for the full frame)
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"

questions.question: What share of shots have camera or virtual-camera motion (zoom, pan, tilt, rotation)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets how often the renderer applies a move.
questions.how_to_answer: From evidence.shots[].camera (video_re_camera_motion: zoom is the natural-log scale change per second, pan_x/pan_y are frame widths/heights per second), count shots with |zoom| > 0.01 or |pan_x| or |pan_y| > 0.01; confirm on F1 at shot start and end for 5 shots.
evidence_required: frames: F1 at shot start and end
questions.challenge: Check the camera estimator on a shot where the subject moves but the frame does not; subject motion must not count.

questions.question: Which move types occur and how often (push-in, pull-out, pan left, pan right, tilt up, tilt down, rotate, parallax, shake, static)?
questions.why_it_matters: Lists moves for the motion vocabulary with weights.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify each shot from camera.zoom sign and pan direction; verify ambiguous ones with F1 first/last frame.
questions.challenge: A combined zoom and pan must be classified once with both components, not counted twice.

questions.question: How fast are zooms (scale change per second, median and range)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the zoom_per_s parameter.
questions.how_to_answer: For zoom shots, scale change per second = exp(camera.zoom) - 1 (camera.zoom is already a log rate per second); cross-check by measuring a feature width on F1 at shot start and end: (w_end / w_start)^(1 / duration_s) - 1.
questions.challenge: Recompute one shot manually from pixel widths; disagreement above 30% questions the estimator.

questions.question: Do zoom directions alternate between consecutive shots (in, out, in, out)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the zoom_alternate rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Write the sign sequence of evidence.shots[].camera.zoom (positive = zoom in); count sign alternations / consecutive pairs.
questions.challenge: Static shots break the sequence; say how they were treated.

questions.question: What easing do moves use (linear, ease-in-out, ease-out, ease-in)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills motion.easing.
questions.how_to_answer: For 3 moving shots, measure a feature position or width on F8-style frames at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% of the shot; compare increments (equal = linear).
evidence_required: frames: 5 samples per shot in 3 shots
questions.challenge: Short shots (under 1 s) cannot show easing reliably; exclude them.

questions.question: Are there punch-ins (instant scale jumps within a shot or on a cut to the same framing) and when do they occur?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds punch-in emphasis to the motion list with timing.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 SSIM across cuts with similar content, or frame steps (F8) showing a one-frame scale change; list timestamps and scale factor.
questions.challenge: Check that a punch-in is not a cut to a different crop of a new asset.

questions.question: Is there camera shake, and what are its amplitude (px) and rough frequency?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a shake effect with parameters.
questions.how_to_answer: Track a fixed point across F8 frames (0.5 s); record max displacement and oscillations per second.
questions.challenge: Handheld footage shake belongs to the footage; say whether it was added in edit (it appears on stills or graphics).

questions.question: How fast are pans as a fraction of frame width per second?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the pan speed parameter.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.shots[].camera.pan_x (already frame widths per second); cross-check one shot by tracking a feature on F1 at start and end: displacement_px / width / duration_s.
questions.challenge: Check the sign convention (positive pan_x = camera moves right, content travels left) and that the feature track agrees within 30%.

questions.question: Does the move start right at the cut or after a delay?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a move start offset.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 over the first 0.5 s of 4 moving shots; find the first frame where the feature moves.
questions.challenge: Convert frames to ms with the true fps from A7.

questions.question: Does motion continue across cuts (the next shot keeps the same direction and speed)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a motion-matching rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare direction and speed of moves in adjacent shots.
questions.challenge: Alternating zooms (004) and matched motion are opposite rules; the answers must be consistent.

questions.question: Is motion filmed (real camera) or virtual (Ken Burns on stills), or both?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the renderer needs footage or can animate stills.
questions.how_to_answer: On moving shots, check for parallax between near and far objects (filmed) versus a uniform scale of a flat image (virtual), using F1 start and end.
questions.challenge: 2.5D parallax on stills mimics filmed motion; look for cut-out edges.

questions.question: Do different layers move at different speeds (parallax), and what is the speed ratio between foreground and background?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills parallax_ratio for 2.5D renders.
questions.how_to_answer: Track a background feature and a foreground feature across the same shot; ratio of displacements.
evidence_required: frames: F1 start/end of parallax shots
questions.challenge: Make sure the foreground is not moving on its own (animation) rather than with the camera.

questions.question: Are rotations used, and how many degrees over how long?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a rotation range to the move vocabulary.
questions.how_to_answer: Measure the angle of a straight edge on F1 at shot start and end.
questions.challenge: Report measured degrees; 'slight rotation' alone is rejected.

questions.question: Are move starts or speed changes aligned with music onsets?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a sync rule for motion keyframes.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare move start times (009) or punch-in times (006) with evidence.audio.onsets_s; share within 80 ms.
questions.challenge: Compare with the chance rate given onset density.

questions.question: What is the maximum zoom factor reached on any shot?
questions.why_it_matters: Bounds zoom so assets are not over-enlarged.
questions.how_to_answer: Max over shots of exp(|camera.zoom| x duration_s), the total scale change across the shot.
questions.challenge: Check the extreme shot by eye; estimators overshoot on blurry frames.

questions.question: Where are zooms centred (subject face, frame centre, text, a detail being explained)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes the zoom focus rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Find the fixed point of the zoom by comparing feature positions between start and end frames.
questions.challenge: Check at least 4 shots before naming a rule.

questions.question: Is motion blur visible during fast moves?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the renderer to add motion blur on fast virtual moves.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 frames during the fastest move; look for directional smearing compared with a static frame.
questions.challenge: Compression blocks on fast motion are not motion blur; check edge direction.

questions.question: Are there speed ramps or slow-motion segments?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds time remapping to the motion vocabulary.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare motion speed of the same subject across frames; look for sudden slow-down (F5 difference drops while motion continues).
questions.challenge: A slow virtual zoom is not slow motion; ramps change the speed of filmed action.

questions.question: Does camera motion pause or slow while dense text is on screen?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a readability rule for moves.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare camera speed in shots with text area_ratio above 0.1 against shots with less text.
questions.challenge: Report the two group medians and their sizes.

questions.question: Is the hook shot's move stronger (faster or larger) than body moves?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a hook-intensity multiplier.
questions.how_to_answer: Ratio of hook zoom_per_s to body median zoom_per_s.
questions.challenge: One hook shot is a single sample; confidence must reflect that.

questions.question: Are there 3D camera moves through layered 2.5D scenes (dolly through cut-out planes)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a 2.5D dolly option.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for layers scaling at different rates during one move (F1 start/end).
questions.challenge: Different-rate scaling can also be separate animations; require consistent depth ordering.

questions.question: Are whip pans used as transitions, and how long are they?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds whip transitions with a duration.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 across cuts with heavy directional blur; count frames of blur.
questions.challenge: Must show directional blur on at least 2 frames.

questions.question: Is there a simulated handheld drift (slow low-amplitude wander) on stills or graphics?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a subtle drift effect.
questions.how_to_answer: Track a feature on F1 frames every 0.5 s across a graphic shot; non-linear wander of a few px suggests drift.
questions.challenge: Linear motion is a pan, not drift.

questions.question: Is there a dominant pan direction (left to right versus right to left) and does it carry meaning (timeline, progress)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a direction rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Count pan directions from camera.pan_x signs.
questions.challenge: Report counts; meaning is inferred and must say so.

questions.question: Does the background layer move independently of the foreground (separate virtual cameras)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills per-layer motion fields.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare border-region motion (evidence.shots[].motion_energy.border, F5 on edges) with foreground scale change.
questions.challenge: A moving background video naturally moves independently; say whether it is a camera move or footage motion.

questions.question: What share of runtime is static (no camera or virtual camera motion), and where do static shots fall?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets where the generator may hold still.
questions.how_to_answer: Sum durations of shots classified static in 002 / duration; list their beat roles.
questions.challenge: Check one static shot with F5 to confirm no slow zoom was missed.

questions.question: Write the Ken Burns rule per shot (start scale, end scale, direction policy, focus point) in terms of parameters.
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a procedural move plan.
questions.how_to_answer: Combine 003, 004, 016 and 015, for example 'scale 1.00 to 1.00 + zoom_per_s x shot_s, alternate in/out, centred on subject, max zoom_max'.
questions.challenge: Apply the rule to 3 observed shots; the predicted end scale must be within 0.03 of the measured one.

questions.question: What range should zoom_per_s take, justified by the observed spread?
questions.why_it_matters: Turns observed speeds into a parameter with an evidence-based range.
questions.how_to_answer: Default = observed median; min/max = observed p25/p75; derived_from camera_motion-003.
questions.challenge: A range wider than observed must be marked assumed.

questions.question: What is the median absolute zoom change per second across all shots from the camera estimator?
questions.why_it_matters: A single motion-intensity number for fidelity scoring.
questions.how_to_answer: Median of |evidence.shots[].camera.zoom| over shots with a non-null estimate (log scale change per second).
questions.challenge: Recompute from evidence.

questions.question: Does any move push the subject or text out of the safe area?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a constraint on move size near frame edges.
questions.how_to_answer: Check end frames of moving shots against the safe box used by the platform lens.
questions.challenge: Cross-check with safe_area.violations timestamps.

questions.question: Do moves follow a subject (tracking) or a fixed path regardless of content?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the renderer needs subject detection for moves.
questions.how_to_answer: Check whether the subject stays at the same frame position during moves in filmed shots.
questions.challenge: Virtual moves on stills are fixed-path by definition unless the focus point changes.

questions.question: Is there a final pull-back or reveal move in the last shots?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds an ending move to the outro.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect camera.zoom on the last 2 shots and F1 start/end frames.
questions.challenge: Make sure the move is not the same alternating pattern as all other shots.

questions.question: Are moves applied to the whole frame or only to inset media inside a fixed layout?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the renderer which layer receives the move.
questions.how_to_answer: Check whether text, borders and backgrounds stay fixed while the photo moves (F1 start/end).
questions.challenge: Look at the frame edges and text positions in both frames.
